source_text: Pridie quam pugnaremus uideo in horomate hoc: uenisse Pomponium diaconum ad ostium carceris et pulsare uehementer. Et exiui ad eum et aperui ei; qui erat uestitus discinctam candidam, habens multiplices galliculas. Et dixit mihi: Perpetua, te expectamus, ueni. Et tenuit mihi manum, et coepimus ire per aspera loca et flexuosa. Uix tandem peruenimus anhelantes ad amphitheatrum, et induxit me in media arena, et dixit mihi: Noli pauere; hic sum tecum et conlaboro tecum. Et abiit. Et adspicio populum ingentem adtonitum. Et quia sciebam me ad bestias damnatam esse, mirabar quod non mitterentur mihi bestiae. Et exiuit quidam contra me Aegyptius foedus specie cum adiutoribus suis pugnaturus mecum. Ueniunt et ad me adolecentes decori adiutores et fautores mei. Et expoliata sum, et facta sum masculus. Et coeperunt me fautores mei oleo defricare, quomodo solent in agonem; et illum contra Aegyptium uideo in afa uolutantem. Et exiuit uir quidam mirae magnitudinis, ut etiam excederet fastigium amphitheatri, discinctatus purpuram inter duos clauos per medium pectus, habens et galliculas multiformes ex auro et argento factas, et ferens uirgam quasi lanista et ramum uiridem in quo erant mala aurea. Et petiit silentium et dixit: Hic Aegyptius si hanc uicerit, occidet illam gladio; haec si hunc uicerit, accipiet ramum istum. Et recessit. Et accessimus ad inuicem et coepimus mittere pugnos; ille mihi pedes adprehendere uolebat, ego autem illi calcibus faciem caedebam. Et sublata sum ab aere, et coepi eum sic caedere quasi terram non calcans. At ubi uidi moram fieri, iunxi manus, ut digitos in digitos mitterem, et adprehendi illi caput, et cecidit in faciem; et calcaui illi caput. Et coepit populus clamare et fautores mei psallere. Et accessi ad lanistam et accepi ramum. Et osculatus est me et dixit mihi: Filia, pax tecum. Et coepi ire cum gloria ad portam Sanauiuariam. Et experrecta sum. Et intellexi me non ad bestias, sed contra diabolum esse pugnaturam; sed sciebam mihi esse uictoriam. Hoc usque in pridie muneris egi; ipsius autem muneris actum si quis uoluerit scribat.
pass_a_gloss: On the day before we were to fight I see in a vision this: that Pomponius the deacon had come to the prison door and was knocking violently. And I went out to him and opened for him; he was dressed in a loose white garment, having many sandals. And he said to me: Perpetua, we are waiting for you, come. And he held my hand, and we began to go through rough and winding places. With difficulty at last we arrived panting at the amphitheatre, and he led me into the middle of the arena, and said to me: Do not be afraid; here I am with you and labor together with you. And he went away. And I look at the huge astonished crowd. And because I knew I had been condemned to the beasts, I was wondering that beasts were not being sent out for me. And there came out against me a certain Egyptian hideous in appearance with his helpers to fight with me. There come also to me beautiful young men, my helpers and supporters. And I was stripped, and I was made male. And my supporters began to rub me with oil, as they are accustomed to do for a contest; and opposite I see that Egyptian rolling in dust. And there came out a certain man of wondrous size, so that he even rose above the top of the amphitheatre, ungirt, with purple between two stripes down the middle of the chest, having also shapely sandals made from gold and silver, and carrying a staff like a trainer and a green branch on which were golden apples. And he asked for silence and said: This Egyptian, if he conquers this woman, will kill her with the sword; she, if she conquers him, will receive this branch. And he withdrew. And we approached each other and began to throw fists; he wanted to seize my feet, but I was striking his face with my heels. And I was lifted into the air, and I began to strike him thus as if not treading the ground. But when I saw delay happening, I joined hands so as to put fingers into fingers, and I seized his head, and he fell on his face; and I trod on his head. And the people began to shout and my supporters to sing. And I approached the trainer and received the branch. And he kissed me and said to me: Daughter, peace with you. And I began to go with glory to the Gate of Life. And I awoke. And I understood that I was going to fight not against beasts, but against the devil; but I knew victory was mine. This much I did up to the day before the games; but the deed of the games themselves, if anyone wishes, let him write.
pass_b_english: On the day before we were to fight, I saw this in a vision. Pomponius the deacon came to the prison door and knocked hard, and I went out to him and opened for him. He wore a loose white robe and many sandals. He said to me, Perpetua, we are waiting for you, come. He took my hand, and we set out through rough and twisting ground. Scarcely at last, out of breath, we reached the amphitheatre, and he led me into the middle of the arena and said to me, Do not fear; I am here with you and I am struggling with you. Then he left. I saw an immense crowd standing in amazement. Because I knew I had been condemned to the beasts, I wondered why no beasts were let loose against me. Then out against me came an Egyptian, foul to look at, with his assistants, to fight me. And to me also came handsome young men, my assistants and supporters. I was stripped naked, and I had become a man. My supporters began to rub me down with oil, as is done before a wrestling match, and across from me I saw that Egyptian rolling in the dust. Then out came a man of wondrous height, so tall that he rose above the roof of the amphitheatre, with his tunic ungirt and purple between two broad stripes down the middle of his chest, and wearing ornate sandals worked in gold and silver, and carrying a staff like a trainer and a green branch bearing golden apples. He called for silence and said, If this Egyptian defeats her, he will kill her with the sword; if she defeats him, she will receive this branch. Then he withdrew.

We closed with each other and began to trade blows with our fists. He tried to grab my feet, while I kept striking his face with my heels. Then I was lifted into the air and began to batter him as if I were not touching the ground. When I saw the bout dragging on, I locked my hands together, lacing finger into finger, and I seized his head, and he fell face down; and I set my heel upon his head. The crowd began to shout, and my supporters began to chant. I went up to the trainer and took the branch. He kissed me and said to me, Daughter, peace be with you. And I began to walk in triumph toward the Life Gate. Then I awoke. I understood that I was to fight not against beasts but against the devil, yet I knew the victory would be mine. This much I have recorded up to the day before the games; as for what happened at the games themselves, let whoever wishes write it.

choices.why: ablative of circumstance; context is a dream before waking, so rendered as vision rather than daytime sight
facta sum with predicate nominative masculus; masculine predicate shows change of sex in the dream, retained literally
accusative of motion toward with proper name of amphitheatre exit for survivors; capitalized as name
